claim: *Commodity intelligence in a governed engineering environment.* General capabilities from a foundation model become useful engineering machinery when connected to an agentic harness and a governed engineering environment. The environment contains both the existing system and the engineering structure used to guide and govern work. Engineers develop and maintain the environment, and may sometimes improve the model through additional training or fine-tuning.
topology: Foundation model and harness exchange outputs/context; harness and GEE exchange actions/results. The trained model enters the harness. Guidance and governance rise from the engineer strip toward their corresponding acting-system columns. A dashed left route returns from the engineer to model development, explicitly qualified by the engineer strip as optional training or fine-tuning.

alt: Model development transforms training data through training into a foundation model. In the acting system, the foundation model exchanges outputs and context with an agentic harness; the harness exchanges actions and results with the governed engineering environment. Four model properties lead to engineering implications: broad reasoning enables delegated implementation; probabilistic output requires assurance; finite working state motivates external representations and retrieval; inexpensive inference enables repeated automated work. The harness supplies tools and integrations, context management, interposition and checks, and parallel or staged execution. The environment includes both the existing system and engineering structure: models, obligations, instructions, procedures, tools, permissions, evidence and controls. The engineer develops and maintains the environment to supply guidance and governance, and may also improve the model through training or fine-tuning.
